text: Bitget Confirms $351.6M Security Incident; Cold Storage Remains Secure Breaking: MLM monitoring indicates that Bitget may be experiencing an ongoing wallet security incident, with three hot wallets and one cold wallet suspected to have been compromised. More than $170 million worth of assets have reportedly been moved out and swapped into ETH, with activity linked to 0x770b10b273fC44Fe9197D6bF20F145c2e98463Ee. The affected wallets are said to still hold about $530 million in assets. The attack vector and total losses remain unconfirmed, and Bitget has not yet publicly responded. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said that at 2:31 p.m. ET on September 24, the exchange detected unauthorized transfers from some hot wallets, with approximately $351.6 million affected. Bitget said its cold wallets remain secure and the breach was limited to portions of its hot and warm wallet layers. User funds are fully covered by the exchange's User Protection Fund, which currently holds more than $464 million. Bitget has flagged the abnormal transfer addresses, notified law enforcement and on-chain security firms, and temporarily suspended withdrawals, while deposits and trading remain operational. The exchange said it will provide hourly updates and publish a full incident report with root-cause analysis and corrective actions within 24 hours. Bitget's security team has preliminarily confirmed that hackers breached a critical backend system of the wallet service, forged transfer details, and triggered the authorized signing process to move funds out; private key leakage has been ruled out. Damage mitigation measures are complete, and there is no further risk of fund loss, though the specific method of intrusion remains under investigation. Bitget CEO Gracy stated during a livestream that while the attacker's identity cannot yet be confirmed with 100% certainty, the incident is highly likely linked to North Korean hackers; certain IP addresses closely match VPN patterns used by a group associated with the DPRK. The current protection fund, exceeding $465 million, is sufficient to cover the losses on its own. In addition to this fund, Bitget holds over $1 billion in proprietary capital. She emphasized that Bitget is certainly not "another FTX" and is fully capable of handling a potential run on withdrawals; noting that Bitget's retail business is comparable in scale to Bybit's, she argued that if Bybit could withstand a $1.5 billion loss, Bitget could certainly absorb a loss of over $300 million. — link
